endorsements.quote: Each application introduced at these stages warrants asking whether it accelerates short-term learning at the cost of competencies that outlast any current tool, and what it does to identity formation.
Education is one layer among others, such as subpopulation testing before deployment and naming accountability for who owns the output of the AI model.

unlisted_practices: Calibrate generative AI integration in medical training to the degree of cognitive displacement and the learner's training stage, rather than prohibiting use.
Defer high-displacement generative AI use, such as generating differentials and plans, for preclinical learners until foundational reasoning competencies are built.
Have learners form their own differential diagnosis before consulting AI, using AI as a check rather than a primary differential generator.
Assess independent reasoning through oral examinations, observed encounters, and written cases that show how a conclusion was reached.
Pair AI-supported knowledge acquisition with synthesis tasks such as case write-ups, oral presentations, and concept mapping.
Require minimum unaided practice, benchmark clinician performance without AI, and use simulation that recreates AI failure to maintain skills.
Issue residency-specific guidance for ambient scribing that protects note-writing as formative reasoning practice.
Set institutional AI guidelines for medical training that name accountability for AI output, specify permitted uses by training stage, and address automation bias directly.
Use AI grading of assessments only in well-defined applications such as OSCE rubric scoring and written clinical reasoning exams, with explicit escalation paths for borderline cases.
Ensure all learners at a given training stage have equal access to AI tools.
Conduct prospective, stage-matched longitudinal studies measuring unaided performance against defined competencies to test deskilling, never-skilling, and mis-skilling risks.
Rely on system design and accountable deployment as primary defenses against automation bias rather than user vigilance alone.

screen.reason: The paper provides a conceptual framework and practical guidance/recommendations for medical educators on governing and integrating generative AI into medical education to mitigate risks like deskilling.
